role_definitions.AUTHORITY: Owns a business decision and is the only writer of that state.
role_definitions.PROJECTION: Deterministically derives a read model from authoritative accepted evidence.
role_definitions.COORDINATOR: Orders work across owners without acquiring their mutation rights.
role_definitions.REPOSITORY: Persists state inside an owning transaction and has no business decision right.
role_definitions.EVIDENCE: Records an observation or proof input without making it accepted truth.
role_definitions.CANDIDATE: May be reviewed or decided but is not active or accepted merely because it exists.
role_definitions.ACCEPTED_FACT: Has crossed its owning acceptance boundary and may feed canonical projections.

semantic_constraints.statement: Book acceptance atomically advances the cursor and binds ChapterOutcome, Canon, Narrative State, long-form projections, audit, and outbox evidence.
An external request that may have started must reconcile durable intent and receipt evidence before any retry.
Draft, Canon extraction, and ChapterOutcome candidate evidence is not visible as accepted actual before Book acceptance.
Raw source material is excluded from production draft context; reusable source knowledge must cross Source and MKAOS governance.
Arc identity is independent of the Volume containment parent chain and one Arc may cross Volumes.
Current code rejects ChapterGroup ranges outside three to eight Chapters, but the repository does not prove this number as a final business invariant.
The runtime currently uses BOOK, VOLUME, ARC, CHAPTER_GROUP, and CHAPTER contracts with strategic, tactical, and operational horizons.
Book Opening currently materializes five durable workflow layers before Book production admission.
Chapter quality thresholds are frozen Capability Pack and quality-profile policy values, not universal domain invariants.
Attempt limits differ by frozen operation definition and runtime policy; only positivity and fenced replay are domain constraints.
Context token ceilings and selection profiles are runtime policy selected per stage and capability.
Quality qualification currently requires at least two evaluator identities; larger counts remain manifest policy.
Pre-hierarchy plan shapes are accepted only through the explicit legacy migration adapter compatibility flag.
Reader Outcome advisory thresholds are hard-coded current behavior without a versioned policy owner.

authority_model.mutation_rule: Project Authority commands commit scoped snapshots and binding decisions.
Only Book Design Authority decides and activates BookDesign versions.
Generation produces candidates; explicit Story Design transitions own semantic activation.
Hierarchical Planning validates plan types and commits active bindings.
Realization proposals require qualification, approval, and freezing before execution evidence.
Approved changes supersede future plan versions without rewriting executed plans.
Book Authority delegates Chapter work and alone accepts its outcome into Book reality.
ChapterGroup records references to child commands and outcomes without copying their execution state.
Chapter Authority commits stage artifacts and terminal candidate evidence under its saga.
Quality decisions require frozen subject, evidence, evaluator, and scope identities.
Extraction is a proposal; Canon approval decides canonical status.

owns: deterministic current narrative state read model
authority_model.mutation_rule: Narrative State is rebuilt only from Book-accepted outcome evidence.
Reader and calibration outputs remain evidence or proposals until another owner decides.
Source and MKAOS stages preserve evidence lineage and source isolation.
Agent Runtime executes bounded contracts and submits candidate or command evidence to domain owners.
Command Kernel ExternalEffect state gates every Provider or object-store send.

owns: runtime job scheduling and claim state
authority_model.mutation_rule: RuntimeJob coordinates claims while the domain Authority owns completion.
Repository writes are valid only inside the owning application and unit of work.

narrative_model.lifecycle_rule: A qualified foundation set binds exact upstream semantic assets for Book Design; it is not chapter truth.
BookDesign candidates may be decided and one version activated; activation establishes design input, not accepted story actual.
A Volume is a typed strategic plan structurally parented by the Book plan.
Segments encode ordered internal progression and state handoffs; they do not form a universal containment parent for Arcs.
An Arc plan has independent identity and may span multiple Volumes.
Arc actual movement is derived from accepted chapter outcomes and cannot be advanced by plan text.
A ChapterGroup is a bounded planning and coordination window, not an execution-state copy.
A Chapter plan is the operational typed plan for one Chapter and remains distinct from its realization and actual outcome.
Scenes and beats are chapter-plan components that schedule state transitions and information flow.
Narrative Realization is a separately approved event-chain contract; it is neither a plan scale nor accepted actual.
A draft remains candidate content through review, revision, quality, and release gates.
A ChapterOutcome becomes accepted actual only in the Book acceptance transaction.
Canon exposes approved or Book-bound accepted facts; extraction alone is not Canon.
Narrative State is a deterministic as-of projection over accepted evidence.
Obligations track setup, due windows, and payoff state across accepted Chapters.
Reader state is proxy, preference, or behavior evidence and cannot mutate accepted facts directly.
